newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel leader wants talks in South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader wants talks in South Africa.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila said on Friday he wanted talks with ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko in South Africa or possibly Zambia and rejected all other proposed venues on security grounds.

"We need to meet the man (Mobutu) in a place where security is 100 percent guaranteed," Kabila told Reuters, adding South Africa or perhaps Zambia were his only preferences for talks on the president's departure from power.
Kabila did not mention Gabon as a venue for the talks, saying he was still prepared to meet Mobutu for face-to-face talks on his "respectful departure from power" but the question was where.
Mobutu's son and spokesman said earlier the president would have no objection to meeting rebel Kabila in Gabon for talks on ending Zaire's civil war.
"There's no official comment yet but it's no problem for the president," Nznaga Mobutu told Reuters when asked about his father's reaction to efforts to stage the talks in Gabon.

Asked when he expected the Mobutu-Kabila meeting could take place, Nzanga said: "The time frame will depend on Mr Mobutu. He has not made any official comment yet, but it will be no problem for him. You know he has said he is in favour of such a meeting."
